How to Read NBA Odds


How NBA Point Spreads Work

Similar to our online sports betting odds for other sports, you will see either a plus sign (+) or a minus sign (-) next to the NBA spreads to indicate the likelihood of that team winning. When you read NBA spreads, the favored team will have a point spread with a minus sign and the underdog team will have a point spread with a plus sign.

For example, the favorite team to win the game could have a spread of -4.5. This means they must win by five or more points to cover the spread. The underdog for the game would be set at +4.5 which means they must lose by less than five points or win the game outright.

For a broader overview, see our complete NBA betting guide.

How NBA Moneylines Work

When making a NBA moneyline bet, or a straight bet, you are betting which team will win outright. American odds use plus and minus signs around a $100 baseline, with negative numbers showing favorites and positive numbers showing underdogs. Because there isn't a point spread, the payout will change based on the moneyline odds. For the favorite, the odds to win is the dollar amount you must bet to get a $100 payout. For the underdog, you must bet $100 to get the odds number as a payout. Here's how it would look if the Boston Celtics are a -145 favorite and the Los Angeles Lakers are a +130 underdog:

  • A $145 bet on the Boston Celtics would win $100 (not including the $145 you wagered)
  • A $100 bet on the Los Angeles Lakers would win $135 (not including the $100 you wagered)

Always compare the price on the same selection across sportsbooks before you bet.

Wagering on the sports betting favorite forces you to bet more money than the potential profit you'll receive. This is called “laying money”. If you are laying money consistently, then you'll need to win these NBA bets over 50% of the time to turn a profit. On spread and total bets, pricing is usually around -110, which reflects the sportsbook's vig or vigorish. The key is separating the odds' implied probability from your own estimate of actual probability.


Basketball Betting FAQs


  • How are NBA betting results determined?

    NBA betting results are based on the statistics provided by the league's governing body (www.nba.com) and the official data supplier.

  • What happens to player props market bets if a player doesn't play?

    If a player doesn't take the court, all bets on that player will be void. Bets stand once a player takes the court, regardless of game time played, and include overtime.

  • Does overtime count for all NBA betting markets?

    Yes, overtime counts for all NBA betting markets unless stated otherwise.

  • How are game props settled?

    Game props are settled based on the player with the most of the relevant statistic. Dead heat rules apply in case of a tie. If a listed player doesn't participate, bets on that player are void. Bets are All-In; if an unlisted player has the highest statistic, all bets are settled as a loss.

How To Read NBA Regular Season Win Totals

In the odds listed above, you'll see a projected number of wins for each team, such as 44.5. That line suggests the approximate number of regular season games the market expects the team to win.

You can then bet:

  • Over 44.5: The team must finish with 45 or more regular season wins.
  • Under 44.5: The team must finish with 44 or fewer regular season wins.

Only games from the regular season count toward NBA win totals. Preseason games, the Play-In Tournament, and the NBA Playoffs do not count. That means wins in the Play-In, Conference Finals, or NBA Finals do not change the result of a regular season win total bet.

The second number shown with the wager is the betting price, displayed with a plus (+) or minus (-) sign. These odds determine the potential payout and can change as the market adjusts its expectations for each team.


What Can Affect NBA Win Total Odds?

Several factors can move NBA win totals during the season:

  • Injuries and health: Missing an important point guard, scorer, defender, or other key player can change the expected number of wins.
  • Roster changes: Trades, free agency, draft picks, and offseason additions can change how competitive a team is expected to be.
  • Young player development: Young players taking on larger roles can improve a team's outlook during the season.
  • Offense and defense: Three-point shooting, defensive rating, rim protection, and overall efficiency can affect expectations.
  • Conference competition: The strength of teams in the Eastern Conference and Western Conference can influence how difficult a team's schedule and playoff race may be.
  • Team performance: A team that starts stronger or weaker than expected may see its win total odds adjust as the season progresses.

NBA Win Totals FAQs

What are NBA win totals?

NBA win total odds are futures bets on how many regular season wins an NBA team will record during the season. FanDuel Sportsbook sets a projected win total for each team, and bettors choose whether the team will finish over or under that number.

A win total line may be a whole number or a fractional number depending on the market. For NBA fans comparing win totals, understanding the line helps show what the market expects from a team over the full NBA season. Injuries, roster changes, offseason moves, free agency, and team performance can all affect the odds. If a whole-number line is offered and the team finishes exactly on that number, the bet is a push and the original stake is refunded.

What does over or under mean for NBA win totals?

The over means you are betting that a team will finish with more regular season wins than the listed total. The under means you are betting that the team will finish with fewer wins than the listed total.

For example, on a win total of 46.5, a team would need at least 47 wins for the over to cash and 46 or fewer wins for the under.

Do NBA playoff or Conference Finals wins count toward win totals?

No. NBA Playoffs, including the Conference Finals and NBA Finals, take place after the regular season and do not count toward regular season win total bets.

Can NBA win total odds change during the season?

Yes. NBA win total odds can change throughout the season based on results, injuries, trades, roster changes, and other developments. A team that performs better or worse than expected may see its win total and betting odds move.

Do injuries affect NBA win totals?

Yes. Injuries can have a major effect on season-long expectations, especially when a team loses an important starter or has several players expected to miss games. Bettors can consider how long players may be out rather than looking only at whether an injury exists.

Can NBA win totals change around the All-Star break?

Yes. By the All-Star break, teams have played a significant part of the regular season, giving the market more information about team performance, health, roster strength, and expected wins. Available win total lines can adjust to reflect that new information.

What team factors can affect regular season win totals?

Team win totals can be influenced by offense, defensive rating, three-point shooting, rim protection, roster depth, coaching, young talent, injuries, and whether key players stay healthy. Offseason changes such as free agency, trades, and draft picks can also affect expectations before and during the season.

Are NBA win totals the same as betting on a team to make the playoffs?

No. A regular season win total bet is based only on how many regular season games a team wins. Whether the team reaches the Play-In Tournament or playoffs is a separate betting market.

How to Read NBA Odds


How NBA Point Spreads Work

Similar to our online sports betting odds for other sports, you will see either a plus sign (+) or a minus sign (-) next to the NBA spreads to indicate the likelihood of that team winning. When you read NBA spreads, the favored team will have a point spread with a minus sign and the underdog team will have a point spread with a plus sign.

For example, the favorite team to win the game could have a spread of -4.5. This means they must win by five or more points to cover the spread. The underdog for the game would be set at +4.5 which means they must lose by less than five points or win the game outright.

How NBA Moneylines Work

When making a NBA moneyline bet, or a straight bet, you are betting which team will win outright. Because there isn’t a point spread, the payout will change based on the moneyline odds. For the favorite, the odds to win is the dollar amount you must bet to get a $100 payout. For the underdog, you must bet $100 to get the odds number as a payout.   • A $100 bet on the Los Angeles Lakers would win $135 (not including the $100 you wagered)
